name: Protocol-Lattice go-agent CodeMode (go-utcp codemode, Expr runtime)
pinned: go-agent ebf73f2b10e26b41266d49535c95303821c2590d (2026-09-30); its go.mod pins go-utcp v1.12.3 (a0edb1984084857cb31f714009c4513451e9b07f); expr-lang/expr v1.17.8; built with go1.27.4 linux/arm64 in Docker
engine: expr-lang/expr, a Go expression language compiled and evaluated in the agent's own Go process (a goroutine per execution). No loops, no statements, no I/O; the only object in scope is `codemode` with CallTool / CallToolStream / Get.
how_run: Go harness run in Docker (Go is not on the host): codemode.NewCodeModeUTCP(fakeClient, nil).Execute(ctx, CodeModeArgs{Code, Timeout: 20000}), the call go-agent's CodeMode.CallTool makes after its LLM planning step (orchestrator.go:44). fakeClient implements UtcpClientInterface.CallTool for lookup.

P1.detail: `let r = codemode.CallTool("lookup", {"id": 21}); r.value` returned 42 in 201 ms, 1 host-side call.

P2.detail: Expr has no print: "unknown name print (1:1)". The value is the only output; `repeat("A", 200000)` came back as one 200000-char string, uncapped. CodeModeResult.Stdout exists but is never set.

P3.detail: "unknown name fetch (1:1)"; `http.Get` gives "unknown name http". The language has no I/O.

P6.detail: Expr has no while loop, so the SPEC form cannot be written. Large ranges die at once on the memory budget (out/P6.jsonl, P6b, P6c). Four nested reduce() over a reused 900-element array ran until Execute returned at 20.0 s with "execution timed out after 20000ms". The evaluation did not stop: 3 s later the goroutine was still alive and RSS had reached 491 MB, because the context is never passed to expr.Run.

P7.detail: map(1..100000, repeat("x", 1e6)) failed in 0.3 ms with "memory budget exceeded"; nested maps likewise (P7b, P7c). This is Expr's DefaultMemoryBudget of 1e6 units, an allocation counter, not a byte limit: the P6 loop reached 506 MB RSS without tripping it.

P8.detail: Second execution: "unknown name kept (1:1)". Each Execute compiles a new program with a fresh env.

P9.detail: map([1..5], codemode.CallTool("lookup", {"id": #})) took 1013 ms, 5 host calls. Expr evaluates sequentially and has no concurrency.

P10.detail: Expr has no throw. A runtime error returns "Expr runtime error: index out of range: 6 (array length is 2) (1:18)" plus the source line and a caret. go-agent's tool handler wraps it as "codemode expression produced an error: ...".

P11.detail: Execute (compile + run) of `1 + 1`: median 0.026 ms, p90 0.034 ms over 20 runs. No setup beyond constructing the struct.

P12.detail: `codemode.client` fails at compile time ("has no field client": unexported). `$env` shows only {codemode}. `type(codemode)` reveals the Go type name. No reflection, imports or host objects reachable; the reachable surface is CallTool on any registered UTCP tool, which is the design.

defaults.time: Execute defaults to 30000 ms (codemode.go:124); go-agent's CodeMode.CallTool passes 20000 (orchestrator.go:44); the generic tool handler defaults to 3000 (codemode.go:148). None stops the evaluating goroutine.
defaults.memory: Expr DefaultMemoryBudget 1e6 allocation units (expr conf/config.go:15), not configurable through go-utcp or go-agent.
defaults.hardened: null: go-agent hard-codes the 20 s timeout on its path and exposes no memory, budget or concurrency option, so no stricter configuration exists.

source_notes.finding: No per-tool functions. One `codemode` object with CallTool(name, args), CallToolStream(name, args) and Get(value, key); the env passed to expr.Compile contains only that object.

Host-side: go-agent ranks UTCP tool specs against the prompt (rankToolSpecs, candidate limit UTCP_CODEMODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT, default 16) and gives only the candidates to a planner LLM, optionally behind the OpenRouter Jev decision layer that picks the exact tool. Generated code is validated to use only those tool names.
Direct in-process Go call into UtcpClient.CallTool with the execution context; results come back as Go values.

The boundary is the language: Expr cannot loop, import, or do I/O, and only `codemode` is in scope. There is no process or memory isolation. The README says to use CodeMode "only in trusted environments", and go-agent refuses codemode.run_code unless AllowUnsafeTools is set.
CodeModeResult{Value, Stdout, Stderr}: Value on success, Stderr holds the error; Stdout is never written.

context.WithTimeout around a goroutine running expr.Run(program, env); on timeout Execute returns but the goroutine keeps evaluating because expr.Run never sees the context. Memory is only Expr's allocation budget.
Expr compile and runtime errors carry (line:col) and a caret excerpt, wrapped as "Expr compilation failed" / "Expr runtime error".

Not general-purpose code: the planner prompt forbids loops and statements, so code mode here is a typed expression pipeline over tool calls. The LLM-planning path needs a model key; the harness skipped it and called Execute directly.

surprises: Code mode here is not a programming language: Expr has no loops, no print, no throw and no concurrency, so the SPEC's infinite loop, print and throw cannot be written as such.
The timeout returns control but never stops the work: the Expr goroutine kept running and growing (491 MB RSS) after Execute returned at 20 s.
Three different default timeouts on three paths: 30 s (Execute), 20 s (go-agent planner path), 3 s (generic tool handler).
The only memory guard is Expr's allocation counter, which a nested reduce bypassed while RSS reached about 500 MB.
Discovery is the most selective seen: deterministic ranking plus an optional external decision model choose candidate tools before the code-writing model sees any schemas.
